notes: Identity: supplied canonical text identifies COLLEGE CHOICE AS A COLLECTIVE DECISION, Nick Huntington-Klein, April 18, 2017, with an author-hosted PDF SOURCE_URL. It contains full manuscript sections, results, references and appendices through manuscript p. 41; it is a primary author manuscript rather than an abstract or secondary article. Title, author and year match the neutral original reference. DOI and published journal pagination are not printed in this text, so exact identity of the final published version is unverified. No PDF path was supplied; no rendering or acquisition was attempted. Target ambiguity: study 1 plus collective decision-making and Table 2 do not select any of fifteen contrasts or distinguish student marginal effect, parent marginal effect and difference. Printed metric is marginal effect, not explicitly identified here as an unstandardized b. Candidates below are preserved without assigning a target or converting metrics. Parent’s/Child’s Opinion Really dislike to Dislike .001 (.004); Dislike to Like .070*** (.010); Like to Love .019*** (.004). Stars identify printed 10%/5%/1% significance levels; exact p values are not given in this table, and no single bound can be assigned without selecting a test. N candidate only for parent field-scope review: explicitly distinct final student and parent age groups in Table 1 give 256 + 228 = 484 respondents for a possible between-group comparison. This does not select the target: a within-student marginal effect has 256 respondents, within-parent 228, while HB estimation uses all 964. Each respondent provides twelve usable choice observations (six per role); 11,568 total observations are not substituted for participant N. Warm-up discarded and dominated choices retained.
